chapter: Sanger, Ben Black and carnival balls
title: The WDSU broadcast and television show with Stardust
summary: He describes his broadcast and TV program, announcing himself, playing Stardust and Blue Skies with dancers.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: And I took it, a $100 bail, I took it, it was a show with my pie. But he had to tell me that I was ornery. When I broadcast for posters on WDSU, I forget, I'm so seldom I have a broadcast. I couldn't get a mix, I couldn't get a test. Every time we were trying to tune up, I said, shh, somebody, I said, well, what are going to do, I'm going to do a broadcast after one, I don't even see a microphone. Because I had music go for 26 weeks and I would set it up myself. I'd see that everything was set to go over the air. I was working for Ballstaff, you know, nice job, 26 weeks. And only a half hour, you've done it quickly. We'd close the curtains and play in nice shirts, sweatshirts. Well because they didn't have any air conditioning. I've been talking about it. I didn't care, they could take all their clothes off, they blew the whole notes, nobody could see us. And I'm telling you, we're kind of bad conditions sometimes. I got to be on it for no reason at all. They brought in a script that long. I said, you're going to read that? They said, yeah. I said, nothing to do it. I said, why? He said, why? I said, if they don't know me now, when are they going to know me? That's recently, you know, I'm retired 11 years. I said, and the announcer, I forget who he is, but he's with the big time now. He said, that's an idea. So we went on to hear, he said, ladies and gentlemen, Holmes presents Johnny the director of his orchestra. He says, no use wasting a lot of time, we can use it for music. Because if you don't know Johnny now, you'll never know him. And that was it. And I went into my program. And I played my program. Ted was listening, Ted the mute? He said, Johnny was fine. I didn't try to put on a production because we only had time to play three numbers. But I liked to play stardust, and if I say so myself, I played it very well on the trumpet. And I would start it with the three pickups, no introduction. Listen to me, you know. Then I had my background like an organ. I predominated, but still I had assistants. You know what I mean? I remember Mrs. Steer, who was a teacher at Royal Eye. Do you know what Mrs. Steer, Ellen Steer? My sister come running into her and said, you want to hear a trumpet player? Come hear this guy. And it's me. She said, that's Johnny Deidre. That's my old friend. I was like, oh, bleh. And for my little novelty, I had a college boy and a college girl, both handsome. They danced the stardust. And the stars would flicker, you know. And that's all the production man. And I closed with blue skies. And gave each of my takeoff men a chance. That was my program. Right after that, we opened up with Somebody Loves Me. With the gestures. You ever see the man doing the gestures? Somebody loves me. I hope it's you. You know, you hold your hand out and you're in there. Yeah. And the boys did it fine. I was out there and they made me, because I could see myself in the monitor, you know. Well, that was out of the book that we did at the dancers. You know, we used to do novelty tunes at dancers, you know. And they all knew the words. Don't think, they didn't have to learn anything for that, for mistakes, you know what I mean? You don't want any mistakes on TV. You want it on, if you're only going to play jatter, play it. Play it right. So I picked out tunes. We knew Somebody Loves Me, and it was kind of an introduction. Somebody loves me, I hope it's you. You know, for me, for me. And I was singing, we'd say, we're all singing, we're doing the gestures. And it's just that if you're listening and you're seeing me, you see, I'm saying, somebody loves me and I hope it's you. It was a pretty fair, accidental introduction. Sounds fine. It sounds fine. And he made a little announcement. I did star rest. This couple came out, they looked splendid. They were dancing under the stars. They knew when the music stopped, they stopped. And they just walked off like a couple were walking. They didn't say anything, a bar like a couple of hams. I said, this is the dance, you're not doing an act. You just glide off.
And he took her on and walked off.
